accepted_examples.german: Du bist bloß drei Jahre älter als ich.
accepted_examples.english: You're only three years older than me.

accepted_examples.german: In dem Teil der Stadt gefällt’s mir nicht.
accepted_examples.english: I don't like that part of town.
accepted_examples.note: Teil means a part or section of the city here.

accepted_examples.german: Wie oft geht die Vier in die Zwölf?
accepted_examples.english: How many times does four go into twelve?
accepted_examples.note: oft occurs in the question word combination wie oft.

accepted_examples.german: Ich kann Tom nicht an den Hörer kriegen.
accepted_examples.english: I can't get Tom on the phone.
accepted_examples.note: kriegen means get/reach someone in this colloquial construction.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist immer noch Blut an der Wand.
accepted_examples.english: There's still blood on the wall.

accepted_examples.german: Du musst es deinen Eltern ja nicht sagen.
accepted_examples.english: You don't have to tell that to your parents.
accepted_examples.note: Eltern means parents and takes the plural form deinen here.
scheinen means shine in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Da wo mein Herz ist, bin ich zuhause.
accepted_examples.english: Home is where the heart is.
accepted_examples.note: Herz means heart in this idiom.

accepted_examples.german: Damals bin ich erst dreizehn Jahre alt gewesen.
accepted_examples.english: I was only thirteen years old at the time.
accepted_examples.note: alt means old in the age expression Jahre alt.

accepted_examples.german: Tom fragte mich, ob er mich wiedersehen dürfe.
accepted_examples.english: Tom asked me if he could see me again.

accepted_examples.german: Wir sind nicht so frei, wie wir denken.
accepted_examples.english: We're not as free as we think.
accepted_examples.note: The example expresses being free/unrestrained, matching the target gloss.

accepted_examples.german: An einem Ort wie diesem ist alles möglich.
accepted_examples.english: Anything could happen in a place like this.
accepted_examples.note: möglich expresses that something can happen/be possible.

accepted_examples.german: Ich wollte Tom nicht so fest schlagen.
accepted_examples.english: I didn't mean to hit Tom so hard.
accepted_examples.note: fest means hard/forcefully in this context.

accepted_examples.german: Ich sehe mich gerade nach einer Waffe um.
accepted_examples.note: Waffe means weapon; the English is a concise rendering of the German search construction.

accepted_examples.english: We barely have any money left.
accepted_examples.note: Kaikki/Wiktionary provides this aligned example for kaum meaning barely/almost no.

accepted_examples.german: Was er sagte, stellte sich als falsch heraus.
accepted_examples.english: What he said turned out to be false.
accepted_examples.note: falsch means false/untrue in this context.

accepted_examples.german: Erinnerst du dich an die Nummer deines Passes?
accepted_examples.english: Do you remember your passport number?
accepted_examples.note: Nummer means a numeric identifier here.
sitzen means sit; the English subject can be singular formal or plural Sie.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist recht wahrscheinlich, dass das, was Tom dir gesagt hat, gar nicht stimmt.
accepted_examples.english: There's a good chance that what Tom told you isn't true.
accepted_examples.note: wahrscheinlich means likely/probable; the translation preserves the likelihood claim.

held_examples.german: Papa sein ist schwerer, als ich dachte.
held_examples.reason: The English translation says parent generically and omits the male/father meaning of Papa; replaced with a gender-specific example.

held_examples.german: Nur neben Tom war noch ein Platz frei.
held_examples.reason: frei means unoccupied/available in this sentence, while this entry's approved gloss is freedom from being enslaved or imprisoned.

held_examples.german: Wie bist du denn auf diese Nummer gekommen?
held_examples.reason: Nummer is idiomatic here (an idea/ploy), not the numeric identifier sense in this entry.

editorial_examples.german: Mein Papa holt mich heute von der Schule ab.
editorial_examples.english: My dad is picking me up from school today.
editorial_examples.note: The translation keeps the specific male-parent meaning of Papa.

plural_reviews.note: Dollars is the plural; after a numeral, currency amounts commonly use invariant Dollar.
plural_reviews.usage_note: The noun plural is Dollars. In prices or amounts after a number, German often uses the unchanged form Dollar (for example, dreißig Dollar).

plural_reviews.note: For the miner sense, the standard plural is Kumpel. Duden also records regional or colloquial alternatives in other uses.
plural_reviews.usage_note: For a miner, use Kumpel as the plural. Kumpels is colloquial mainly for the companion/friend sense; Kumpeln is an Austrian alternative.

plural_reviews.value: No regular plural in the everyday air/atmosphere sense
plural_reviews.note: Duden marks the ordinary air and atmosphere senses as without a plural; Lüfte belongs to poetic wind/air-current senses.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Luft meaning the air or atmosphere is normally uncountable. Lüfte is poetic or literary for breezes/air currents, not the everyday plural.

plural_reviews.note: Onkel is standard; Onkels is colloquial.
plural_reviews.usage_note: The standard plural is Onkel. Onkels is a colloquial alternative.

plural_reviews.note: Duden gives Partys as the plural.
The feminine typesetting noun Type has plural Typen.
Stücke is the plural for countable pieces/items; Stück also appears unchanged as a measure word.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Stücke for several pieces or items. In measure expressions, the singular form Stück can remain unchanged (for example, fünf Stück).

plural_reviews.value: No plural in the intended light-as-radiation sense
plural_reviews.note: The visible-light/radiation senses are marked without plural; Lichter refers to separate light sources, and Lichte is a special or older form.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Licht as visible radiation or general illumination is normally singular-only. Lichter means separate lamps/light sources; Lichte is an older/poetic variant or a plural for candles.

plural_reviews.note: Reste is the standard plural; Rester is commercial and Resten Swiss regional.
Sinne is used for perceptual faculties; meanings such as a word's sense are normally singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Sinne for sensory faculties (the five senses). Sinn meaning a word's meaning or purpose is usually singular.

plural_reviews.note: Böden applies to countable grounds, floors or soil types; some abstract/material senses are singular-only.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Böden for separate floors, patches of ground or soil types. Soil/ground as a material or abstract basis is often singular.

plural_reviews.note: Münder is the ordinary plural; Munde and Münde are rare alternatives.
Läden is the usual plural for shops; Laden is less common in some senses.
Both Generale and Generäle are accepted plurals for officers holding the rank; the rank itself is singular-only.
plural_reviews.usage_note: For people with the rank, both Generale and Generäle are used. The rank/title General itself is normally singular-only.

plural_reviews.note: Rums is standard; Rume is an Austrian regional variant.
Biere counts varieties/sorts; servings often use invariant Bier.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Biere for different kinds or varieties of beer. A serving is often counted with unchanged Bier (for example, zwei Bier).

plural_reviews.note: Rollen is the plural for rolls/reels/spools.
Hochzeiten is the plural for weddings.
Fotos is the standard plural.
The dictionary's declension table marks Weile as having no plural. The form Weilen in zuweilen is a frozen dative plural, not the ordinary noun plural.
